why: Grants (FY2024) for healthcare clinics and access to care for low-income uninsured people, including several free clinics.
Funds free dental care for the uninsured (FY2024), partly through free clinics, but it is dental rather than medical care.
Only 5 grants (FY2023), mostly to Sisters of Mercy Urgent Care and a council on aging, with one $50k grant to ABCCM's free clinic for the uninsured.
Only one $7.4k grant in five years, to a family services agency, so it is not a meaningful funding source.
Repeated grants (FY2025) for care of the medically uninsured, to free programs such as Gratis Healthcare, St Anne's Free Medical Program and Volunteers in Medicine.
All 374 grants (FY2024) fund healthcare for the uninsured and underinsured at clinics such as CommunityHealth, Care Ring and Grace Medical Home.
All 220 grants (FY2024) support services to uninsured patients at Ohio free clinics and a charitable pharmacy.
Access-to-care grants (FY2024) with free clinics as top recipients, e.g. $2.28M to Lloyd F Moss Free Clinic and $300k to Guadalupe Free Clinic.
253 grants (FY2024) to North Carolina member free clinics to expand healthcare for the uninsured.
Broad Tulsa health and human-services funder; clinic care for the uninsured appears only in a few women's health and breast care grants.
